text:
anya: FYI onboarding sample app flaky on Android 12: sometimes first call returns, subsequent 'fetch models' taps hit SocketTimeoutException. Stack mentions okhttp3.internal.http2.StreamResetException and 'timeout on read' in logs. Anyone seen this pattern with our SDK?

sam: Are you using the repo's OkHttpClient or creating a new client per request? Also, which OkHttp version and is retryOnConnectionFailure enabled?

anya: Using sample-app default client code + our auth interceptor/Authenticator. OkHttp 4.9.3 in the sample. `retryOnConnectionFailure(true)` is set. Repro on Pixel 4a Android 12 emulator and physical device.

liam: Two common culprits: (1) infinite readTimeout (readTimeout(0)) combined with older Android HTTP stack oddities, (2) Authenticator replays for non-idempotent bodies + retry wrapper recreating request body incorrectly. Are we rebuilding streaming bodies when the Authenticator retries?

anya: We set readTimeout(0) to avoid cutting long streams during generation. The auth Authenticator attempts to re-auth and replay the original request by cloning it. If body is a one-shot streaming request it may fail.

sam: readTimeout(0) -> infinite reads can produce odd socket behavior on some Android releases. Try explicit 2 minute read timeout and ensure single OkHttpClient instance. Also, when using Authenticator, prefer to implement token-refresh by returning a new request that DOES NOT replay streaming bodies or mark them non-replayable. Quick local patch: 

```
OkHttpClient client = new OkHttpClient.Builder()
  .connectTimeout(15, TimeUnit.SECONDS)
  .readTimeout(2, TimeUnit.MINUTES)
  .retryOnConnectionFailure(true)
  .authenticator(myAuthenticator)
  .build();
```

liam: Also validate that the sample doesn't create the client inside the button handler. If it's recreated per click, connection reuse is lost and HTTP/2 streams reset more frequently. Make client a singleton in the Application class.

anya: Tried: switch to singleton client, readTimeout 2m, and temporarily set `retryOnConnectionFailure(false)` -> stable across 10+ runs on emulator Android 12 and Pixel 4a. Re-enabling retryOnConnectionFailure seemed okay after the other changes. Conclusion: combination of infinite read timeout + per-request client + Authenticator replay was the trigger.

deploy-bot: Created issue #2410: "sample-app: infinite readTimeout + per-request OkHttpClient + Authenticator replay causes intermittent SocketTimeoutException on Android 12" https://github.com/redwood-inference/sample-apps/issues/2410

sam: Can you add a short troubleshooting note in the sample README about not using readTimeout(0) on Android, making OkHttpClient a singleton, and caution about replaying non-idempotent bodies from Authenticator? Maybe include the code snippet for safe client creation. :thumbsup:

anya: Yep I'll open a PR with sample changes, README blurb, and a small unit test that ensures client is reused. PR will reference issue #2410. Thanks! :rocket:
